tips.details: Create proper drainage channels to prevent waterlogging. Check and repair field bunds regularly.
Pest incidence increases in monsoon. Use sprayers to protect crops from fungal diseases and pests.
Plan farm operations between rain intervals. Use alternate rows for irrigation optimization.
Grow monsoon crops like rice, maize, cotton, and pulses. Avoid early sowing to prevent crop damage.
Use organic mulch to prevent soil erosion and conserve moisture during heavy rains.
Sow rabi crops at proper time - wheat in October-November, pulses in October.
Plan irrigation based on crop demand. Winter crops need 2-3 irrigations depending on rainfall.
For sensitive crops, monitor frost warnings. Use smoke or irrigation to prevent frost damage.
Winter weeds are more problematic. Apply pre-emergent herbicides and maintain field cleanliness.
Apply nutrients at proper time. Use foliar spray for micronutrients if deficiencies appear.
Increase irrigation frequency. Use drip irrigation to save water. Check soil moisture regularly.
Use mulching to reduce soil temperature. Provide adequate water, especially during flowering.
Grow heat-tolerant crops. Summer vegetables like okra, brinjal, cucumber are ideal.
Higher pest incidence in summer. Use shade nets and regular monitoring to reduce pest population.
After winter crop harvest, prepare land properly. Add organic matter and correct pH before sowing.

title: Drought Management
description: Strategies to cope with drought conditions

tips.details: Choose drought-tolerant varieties. Millets, pulses, oilseeds are suitable for drought areas.
Construct farm ponds, bunds, and contour trenches to capture rainwater.
Apply 5-10cm organic mulch to reduce evaporation and maintain soil moisture.
Add organic matter to increase water holding capacity. Practice deep ploughing.
Reduce nitrogen, increase potassium for drought tolerance. Use organic manure.

title: Flood Management
description: Strategies to protect crops from flooding

tips.details: Create raised beds for vegetable crops. Maintain proper drainage channels.
Select flood-tolerant crop varieties. Avoid crops sensitive to waterlogging.
Remove excess water immediately after flooding. Use pump sets if necessary.
Check for soil pH changes. Monitor nutrient deficiencies and pest outbreaks.
Document crop loss and file claims under PMFBY within specified time frame.
